chunks: And know that this world is the place of trial.
Whoever here wastes any hour of his time will repent it on the Day of Judgement,
and nothing can ever make you free of need of what is right.
One of the rights on you is that you should protect yourself (from sins) and look after the subjects to your best.
The benefit that will come to you from this will be greater than that which will accrue (to people) through you;
and that is an end to the matter.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, the lower realm of existence
key_terms.الرَّعِيَّةِ: The subjects or people under governance

ai.seo_question: What are the key duties of a governor according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this letter to the governor of Hulwan, Imam Ali (AS) contextualizes worldly governance as a spiritual trial where every moment of leisure becomes a source of regret, urging the ruler to prioritize self-accountability and diligent care for his subjects. This reflects the Shia concept of *adab al-dawla* (etiquette of governance), where the leader’s personal piety and justice are the foundation of societal well-being, ensuring that the ruler’s spiritual merit exceeds the material distribution to the populace.
